name: Internal Deployment Disclosure
summary: The lab tells the public or governments when it uses a much more capable model internally before, or without, a public release.
description: The most capable models are often used inside the lab months before release, for example to write code and do research. Without disclosure, nobody outside the lab knows about these models or their risks.

criteria.label: Notification
criteria.description: The lab reports internal deployment of each new frontier model.

criteria.label: Timely
criteria.description: The report comes within a set time after internal use starts.

criteria.label: Capabilities
criteria.description: The report includes dangerous-capability evaluation results.

criteria.label: Safeguards
criteria.description: The report tells the safeguards and monitoring for internal use.

orgs.summary: California law requires OpenAI to give the state regular confidential summaries of internal-use risk. OpenAI disclosed that unreleased Astra may reach Critical cyber capability.

events.title: California law requires internal-use risk summaries
events.summary: SB 53 takes effect. Large frontier developers must send the state emergency office a summary of their catastrophic-risk assessments of internal use every three months, or on a reasonable schedule they set.

quote.text: The systemic risk assessment and mitigation processes described here apply to covered models that OpenAI has deployed externally, and in some cases internally with respect to risks resulting from circumventing oversight mechanisms.

sources.title: SB-53 Artificial intelligence models: large developers.
Transparency in Frontier AI Act Reporting
sources.publisher: California Governor's Office of Emergency Services

events.title: Discloses unreleased Astra may reach Critical cyber level
events.summary: Says preliminary evidence shows its upcoming model Astra may meet the Critical cybersecurity threshold. Describes the monitoring and security it now requires for internal training and use of such models.

quote.text: preliminary evidence that one of our upcoming models, Astra, may meet the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold under our Preparedness Framework

sources.title: Pacing model development in an era of cyber-critical capabilities

notification.commitment: Confidential internal-use risk summaries to California; disclosed unreleased Astra once.
notification.missing: Only one public disclosure, by its own choice; state summaries are confidential.

timely.commitment: Law requires summaries every three months or on a schedule OpenAI sets.
timely.missing: No time limit for public disclosure.

capabilities.commitment: Astra post gave preliminary Critical cyber evidence.
capabilities.missing: No detailed results; outside results came only at public release.

safeguards.commitment: Astra post describes required monitoring and security for internal training and use.
safeguards.missing: No regular public report on internal safeguards.

orgs.summary: Anthropic says it will publish analysis within 30 days of a much riskier internal model (misalignment, AI R&D). It disclosed unreleased Model 2 in 2026.

events.title: Promises U.S. government notice above ASL-2
events.summary: RSP 2.0 says it will notify a U.S. government entity if a model needs more than ASL-2 protections. If it does not release such a model, it will likely share evaluation details with the government instead.

quote.text: We will notify a relevant U.S. Government entity if a model requires stronger protections than the ASL-2 Standard.

events.title: California law requires internal-use risk summaries
events.summary: SB 53 takes effect. Large frontier developers must send the state emergency office a summary of their catastrophic-risk assessments of internal use every three months, or on a reasonable schedule they set.

sources.title: SB-53 Artificial intelligence models: large developers.
Transparency in Frontier AI Act Reporting
sources.publisher: California Governor's Office of Emergency Services

sources.title: Our compliance framework for California's SB 53

events.title: Adds public reports on riskier internal models
events.summary: RSP 3.0 says Risk Reports every 3 to 6 months cover internal models with significant added risk, with a public discussion within 30 days of finding one. The U.S. government notice is no longer in the policy.

quote.text: Within 30 days of determining that we have an internally deployed model that is in-scope (per the description above), we will publish a discussion (in a System Card or elsewhere) of how that model’s capabilities and propensities affect or change the analysis in the Risk Report.

events.title: Limits internal-model trigger to misalignment and AI R&D
events.summary: RSP 3.3 says the 30-day public discussion applies to internal models whose misalignment or automated R&D risks significantly exceed those of models it has already analyzed in public. Other risk areas no longer trigger it.

quote.text: Within 30 days of determining that we have an internally deployed model that (1) could pose risks related to high-stakes misalignment or automated R&D that (2) significantly exceed those of all models for which we have publicly analyzed such risks

events.title: Risk Report discloses three unreleased internal models
events.summary: The August 2026 Risk Report says three internal models with frontier or near-frontier capabilities were not public as of July 15, 2026. One, Model 2, has no planned release.

quote.text: As of the coverage date of July 15, 2026, there were three internal models with frontier or near-frontier capabilities which had not been publicly released

notification.commitment: August 2026 Risk Report listed three unreleased internal models.
notification.missing: Policy covers only models with much higher misalignment or AI R&D risk.

timely.commitment: Public discussion within 30 days of deciding a model is in scope.
timely.missing: Clock does not start at first internal use; not independently checked.

capabilities.commitment: August 2026 Risk Report gives results for unreleased Model 2, such as SHADE-Arena.
capabilities.missing: No outside results published for these models.

safeguards.commitment: Risk Reports describe internal-use safeguards; August 2026 report details usage monitoring.

orgs.summary: Google's framework says it aims to share information with governments when a model reaches a critical capability level. It sets no time limit.

events.title: Aims to tell governments of critical-level models
events.summary: Frontier Safety Framework 2.0 says that if a model reaches a critical capability level with unmitigated public-safety risk, it aims to share model information, evaluation results and mitigation plans with government authorities.

quote.text: If we assess that a model has reached a CCL that poses an unmitigated and material risk to overall public safety, we aim to share information with appropriate government authorities

events.title: Adds safeguards for large-scale internal deployments
events.summary: Frontier Safety Framework 3.0 extends deployment mitigations and risk review to large-scale internal deployments, mainly for machine learning R&D risk. The terms for sharing information with governments do not change.

quote.text: deployment mitigations focus on different threat models and therefore also include measures for large scale internal deployments

sources.title: Google DeepMind strengthens the Frontier Safety Framework

notification.commitment: Aims to share information with governments at a critical capability level with unmitigated risk.
notification.missing: Not for each new internal model.

timely.missing: No time limit found for sharing with governments.

capabilities.commitment: Shared information may include evaluation results.
capabilities.missing: Only for critical-level models and where Google finds it appropriate.

safeguards.commitment: Mitigations for high-risk internal deployments; disclosures may include mitigation plans.

orgs.summary: Meta's framework says it will regularly give relevant authorities summaries of internal-use risk, as appropriate. It names no authority or schedule.

events.title: Promises internal-use risk reports to authorities
events.summary: Framework 2.0 says it will regularly assess catastrophic risk from internal use of frontier models and, as appropriate, give relevant authorities a summary. Version 2.1, published October 2026, keeps this text.

quote.text: We will also regularly assess the potential for catastrophic risk from internal use of Frontier AI models and, as appropriate, provide relevant authorities with a summary of these assessments through an internal-use risk report.

notification.commitment: Will give relevant authorities internal-use risk summaries, as appropriate.
notification.missing: Names no authority; no public report.

timely.commitment: Says it assesses internal-use risk regularly.
timely.missing: No schedule or deadline for reports to authorities.

capabilities.commitment: Reports will rely on monitoring and preparedness evaluations.
capabilities.missing: Reports go only to authorities, as appropriate.

safeguards.commitment: Reports will rely on monitoring tied to internal deployment threat models.

orgs.summary: California law requires xAI to give regular confidential internal-use risk summaries. xAI's June 2026 framework dropped its internal-use review text and California reference.

events.title: California law requires internal-use risk summaries
events.summary: SB 53 takes effect. Large frontier developers must send the state emergency office summaries of internal-use catastrophic-risk assessments every three months. The December 2025 framework says it complies with this law.

quote.text: For internal use, we review catastrophic risks like oversight evasion before extensive rollout.

sources.title: SB-53 Artificial intelligence models: large developers.
Transparency in Frontier AI Act Reporting
sources.publisher: California Governor's Office of Emergency Services

events.title: Framework update drops internal-use risk review text
events.summary: The June 2026 framework no longer says xAI reviews catastrophic risks of internal use before extensive rollout, and no longer cites California's law. The law still requires internal-use summaries.

sources.title: xAI rewrote and shortened its Frontier AI Framework

notification.commitment: California law requires confidential internal-use risk summaries to the state.
notification.missing: Not public; xAI's June 2026 framework does not mention them.

timely.commitment: Law requires summaries every three months or on a reasonable xAI schedule.

capabilities.commitment: Summaries cover catastrophic-risk assessments of internal use.
capabilities.missing: Confidential; no public evaluation results for internal models found.

safeguards.missing: No statement found on internal-use safeguards or monitoring reports.
